claim: Feature flags add a configuration dimension within one deployed release, which lets teams expose different code paths without separate environments.
A flag can turn risky code off without a full deployment and can support production measurement before broader release.
For fast agent teams, merging code and enabling it for production users should be separate permissions.
The speakers propose testing changes against production-shaped data before enabling them, then activating a flag for a short time or a small cohort.
Flag decisions need collected metrics that can trigger rollback or wider rollout.
Abandoned experiments leave stale flags and add codebase complexity, so flag cleanup is part of the operating process.
